item.title: Closing arguments read in social media addiction trial
item.description: Closing arguments were delivered in a first of it's kind social media addiction trial. The jurors, who will decide if Meta and YouTube are liable for getting teens addicted to social media, heard from experts and even Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

item.title: 'This place broke something in us': Kids languish in ICE detention long past 20-day limit
item.description: ICE is not supposed to detain children for longer than 20 days under a decades-old court settlement. The Trump administration has routinely violated that limit.

item.title: New Iranian supreme leader vows vengeance in fiery first statement
item.description: Iran's new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, broke his silence Thursday after four days of rumors that he had been injured in an airstrike.

item.title: Rescue efforts underway after U.S. refueling plane crashes in Iraq
item.description: U.S. Central Command says a KC-135 refueling aircraft went down in “friendly airspace” in western Iraq and was not brought down by hostile or friendly fire. Rescue operations are underway as Iran escalates attacks on oil tankers and threatens to close the Strait of Hormuz. NBC News’ Richard Engel reports.

item.title: Trump touted falling gas prices but now says 'we make a lot of money' as they go up
item.description: President Donald Trump says all the time that gas prices are dropping on his watch, but with the Iran war, he says rising oil costs are good for America.

item.title: In Tehran, hope for change turns to panic: 'They are turning the country into ruins'
item.description: Hoda was so furious over Iran’s violent crackdown on protesters in January that she wanted the country’s security forces to be attacked as payback.

item.title: Armed man rams vehicle into Michigan synagogue; being investigated as possible terrorism
item.description: A man with a rifle drove a vehicle into Temple Israel Synagogue in West Bloomfield, Michigan today. He was able to drive down a hallway before being taken down by security guards who opened fire. No staff or children were injured. Investigators are now looking into this as possible terrorism. NBC News’ Ty Steele has the story.

item.title: Deadly campus shooting investigated as act of terrorism
item.description: A gunman opened fire at Old Dominion University, killing one and injuring two others. The shooting is now being investigated as an act of terrorism. NBC News' Ryan Nobles reports from Newport News, Virginia.
